title: Clear the hair from under a sink's open pop-up stopper: feed the hooked wand in under its head and draw the hair out
instruction: Clear the hair from under the sink stopper, then leave the tool and the hair on the counter.
context: Hair caught below a bathroom sink's pop-up stopper is the usual reason a sink drains slowly. Hooked wands such as the Drain Weasel are sold to clear it without taking the drain apart; the maker says the wand "will slide past most drain pop-up stoppers". The hair is out of sight and out of reach: the open stopper's head covers the drain, so the thin wand has to go in under its edge, bend down the bore beside the stopper and come back out with the hair.
setup: Metres; x forward from the line through the arm bases, y to the robot's left, heights above the robot's table top. Vanity (fixed): 31 x 22 in (787 x 559 mm) stone top, 30 mm thick, surface 243 mm up, front edge x 0.105, left end y 0.3735, right end y -0.4135; closed cabinet below, cut off at the table top; wall and 100 mm backsplash behind; single-hole faucet behind the basin, spout 110 mm above the top. Basin: Kohler Caxton K-2205 under-mount vitreous china (432 x 356 mm oval opening, long side along y; 162 mm water depth; 44 mm drain hole; no overflow), drain at (0.360, -0.020). Drain: Kohler K-7114 pop-up without overflow, chrome brass; 54 mm flange 4 mm proud, top 55 mm up; 32 mm bore (est.); 3/16 in pivot rod from the back, 50 mm below the flange top (est.), through the stopper's eye; tailpiece cut off at the table top. Stopper (fixed, open): domed head 42 mm across (est.), underside 20 mm above the flange (est.); 36 mm gasket; four dark guide fins 30 mm across, 2 mm thick, at 30 and 120 degrees from +x (est.; the rod through the stopper's eye sets its turn); 9 mm stem. Hair: 0.50 g of 150 mm human hair (from a human-hair weft), wet, wound three turns round the stem among and below the fins and over the rod, filling the bore 22 to 52 mm below the flange top. Tool (loose): FlexiSnake Drain Weasel PLUS, orange reusable handle 133 mm (est.: 45 mm sleeve 30 mm square, 26 mm grip, 30 mm cap) with a 12 in (305 mm) wand (current refills are 18 in: trim one to 305 mm at its handle end), 3 mm thick, last 32 mm a dark 6 mm hooked pad; 56 g in the simulation (est.). Lot A: lying on the top's front strip along its front edge, wand pointing to the robot's right, the wand's end of the handle at (0.135, 0.3285), axis 15 mm above the stone; the handle reaches 88 mm past the top's left end. Lot B: the tool 20 mm further right. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Score 0 if at any time the tool drops off the vanity (any part more than 20 mm below the countertop outside the vanity's outline). Otherwise, at the end, with both grippers 10 mm or more from the tool and the tool still for the last 1 s, where 'the hair' is at least 0.40 g of the 0.50 g clump at the place named (weighed dry, 0.01 g scale) and 'at the countertop's height' means inside the vanity's outline, no lower than 10 mm under the stone's surface (on the stone, or on the pad where the wand's end reaches past the rim): 1.0 the hair out of the drain and at the countertop's height and the whole tool lying on the countertop (sleeve on the stone; every point between 10 mm below and 40 mm above the stone's surface, none hanging into the basin); 0.5 the hair out of the drain and at the countertop's height but part of the tool in the basin; 0.25 the hair out of the drain (outside the flange, or 10 mm or more above its top) but not at the countertop's height (in the basin, or dropped past the top's edge); else 0. Read from a top photo, a straightedge across the rim with a ruler, the scale, and the video for release and stillness. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz) per lot
reset_notes: 1. Under the basin undo the pivot nut, draw the rod out of the stopper's eye, lift the stopper out; clear and weigh any hair left. 2. Wind a wet 0.50 g bundle of 150 mm human hair three turns round the stopper's stem under its fins, refit the stopper, push the rod back through its eye and the hanging hair, refit the nut. 3. Lift rod down: stopper fully open (head 20 mm above the flange). 4. Fit a new wand (18 in refill trimmed to 305 mm at its handle end). 5. Lay the tool at its lot's marks (wand to the right, its handle's wand end 45 mm (A) or 65 mm (B) in from the top's left end); check it rests untouched 10 s. 6. Arms at ready. Run with -E object_jitter=0.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The wand's last 128 mm is eight 16 mm spring-hinged links (stiffness estimated, 2 g each) bending in one plane. The hair is a declared rule, drawn but not colliding: taken once the hooked pad has spent 0.5 s in the clump and is drawn up 10 mm in the bore, then carried whole on the pad; tangle and pull-out force are not simulated. Access is simulated: the 42 mm head covers the 32 mm bore. No water or handle spin. Stopper fixed open. Vanity on the robot's table, cabinet cut there.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lot A 0.0, lot B 0.0); demo: 1.0 (lot A 1.0, lot B 1.0)
